subject: .rst file not produced during production run

messages.author: Roberts, Amy L2
messages.body:
Hello,
I'm trying to simulate a box of water as part of a student lab, but am finding that when I run the production step no .rst file is produced as output.
The command I am running is
$AMBERHOME/bin/sander -O -i 4_md.in -o wat_md.out -p wat.prmtop -c wat_equil.rst -r wat_md.rst -x water.mdcrd
And the contents of my 4_md.in are
&cntrl
imin = 0, irest = 1, ntx = 7,
ntb = 2, pres0 = 1.0, ntp = 1,
taup = 2.0,
cut = 9.287, ntr = 0,
ntc = 2, ntf = 2,
tempi = 300.0, temp0 = 300.0,
ntt = 3, gamma_ln = 1.0,
nstlim = 20000, dt = 0.001,
ntpr = 100, ntwx = 1, ntwr = 1000
/
The minimization, defrost, and equilibration steps _seem_ to have gone according to plan.
Has anyone encountered an issue like this before? Is there additional information that would be useful for troubleshooting?
Thanks,
Amy
Assistant Professor of Physics
CU Denver | Downtown Campus

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Apr 16, 2021, Roberts, Amy L2 wrote:
>
>Cutoff list exceeds largest sphere in unit cell!!
> Big problems with imaging!!
> a,b,c = 24.047116319114011 22.573755462423588 27.547999941411810
> alpha,beta,gamma = 90.000000000000000 90.000000000000000 90.000000000000000
> cutlist,sphere = 11.287000000000001 11.286877731211792
You have a very small box size...very near the limit for Amber.
You need to reduce your cutoff for such a small cell. I'm guessing(?) that
you set cut=9.287 in response to earlier messages like this. But with
constant pressure, the cell size will decrease, and with it, the largest
value of cut that you can use.
If this is "just" a student project, using the default cut of 8.0 should be
fine for teaching. If you need to explore bigger cutoffs, you'll need to
construct a bigger box.
....hope this helps...dac

messages.author: Roberts, Amy L2
messages.body:
Yes, setting the cut to 8.0 resolves this issue!
The command that now succeeds is
$AMBERHOME/bin/sander -O -i 4_md.in -o wat_md.out -p wat.prmtop -c wat_equil.rst -r wat_md.rst -x water.mdcrd
And per your suggestion I updated the contents of my 4_md.in to
&cntrl
imin = 0, irest = 1, ntx = 7,
ntb = 2, pres0 = 1.0, ntp = 1,
taup = 2.0,
cut = 8.0, ntr = 0,
ntc = 2, ntf = 2,

ntt = 3, gamma_ln = 1.0,
nstlim = 20000, dt = 0.001,
ntpr = 100, ntwx = 1, ntwr = 1000
/
Thank you!
Amy
